nodes.summary: The decision problem GENERALIZED ASSIGNMENT accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of generalized-assignment instances, to an instance that is well formed and feasible. Bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.
nodes.title: The generalized assignment decision problem

nodes.summary: Let $(R, C, c, K)$ be a generalized-assignment instance, let $n$ be the number of rows of $R$ (the jobs) and $m$ the length of $c$ (the machines), and read entries missing from $R$ or $C$ as $0$. The instance is feasible when there are machines $a_1, \dots, a_n \in \{1, \dots, m\}$ such that for every machine $i$ the sum of $R_{j,i}$ over the jobs $j$ with $a_j = i$ is at most $c_i$, and…
nodes.title: Feasible generalized assignments

nodes.summary: A generalized-assignment instance is a tuple $(R, C, c, K)$ where $R$ and $C$ are finite lists of finite lists of natural numbers, read as matrices indexed by job and machine ($R_{j,i}$ is the resource job $j$ consumes on machine $i$ and $C_{j,i}$ is the cost of assigning job $j$ to machine $i$), $c$ is a finite list of natural numbers (the machine capacities $c_i$), and $K$ is a natural number (the cost bound).
nodes.title: Generalized-assignment instances

nodes.summary: The generalized assignment decision problem belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
nodes.title: GENERALIZED ASSIGNMENT is NP-complete

nodes.summary: A generalized-assignment instance $(R, C, c, K)$ is well formed when $R$ and $C$ have the same number of rows and every row of $R$ and every row of $C$ has as many entries as $c$ (one per machine).
nodes.title: Well-formed generalized-assignment instances

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
